clue.text: Kid who's cheeky with a photographer inhales joint

indicators.note: to inhale is to take something inside, so one piece is drawn into the rest

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for with
the hip is a joint of the body
a, as in 'once a day', means per
a snapper is informal for a photographer

explanation.surface: A cheeky youngster tags along with a press photographer who is smoking a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: The joint goes in after the first letter of the whole string. 'Joint' looks like cannabis in the surface but is a body part; 'a' for per is as in 'twice a day'.
explanation.definitionFit: A whippersnapper is an impertinent young person, a cheeky youngster who oversteps.

clue.text: Old ill-natured sheep, as stated in report

indicators.note: something stated is spoken, so the sound of the words counts rather than spelling

blocks.note: wry once meant perverse or ill-natured, now an archaic sense
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A report describes a grumpy old ram.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, WRY TUP runs together as WRITE-UP; the sound split differs from the spelling split.
explanation.definitionFit: A write-up is a written account or review of an event, such as a newspaper report.

clue.text: Console jury members south of Fife, perhaps

blocks.note: a fife is a small flute, an example of an instrument
a jury panel is the group of people chosen to serve

explanation.surface: Comfort jurors from south of the Scottish county of Fife.
explanation.walkthrough: Fife is also a Scottish county, which drives the geographic surface; 'south of' puts PANEL below INSTRUMENT in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A console is the dashboard of controls and dials in a vehicle or machine, also called an instrument panel.

clue.text: Excuse firm departing from purpose

indicators.note: leaving a word means those letters are taken out of it

blocks.note: pleasure as in 'what is your pleasure?', one's will or purpose
sure means firm or steady, as in a sure footing

explanation.surface: A company's alibi for abandoning its aims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' suggests a company but means secure; take SURE from PLEASURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is a reason offered in defence or justification, so it is an excuse.

clue.text: Pretty? Yes, indeed!

blocks.note: first meaning: as an adverb, fairly or somewhat
second meaning: an old-fashioned British exclamation of emphatic agreement

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' reads as an adjective about looks, but it is the adverb, as in 'pretty good'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather means fairly ('rather cold'), and 'Rather!' is dated British slang for an enthusiastic yes.

clue.text: Wedding, tailor plans it around second of June

indicators.note: to tailor is to alter and refit, so the letters are reworked
the second of a word is its second letter only

blocks.note: taken as written
the second letter of June

explanation.surface: A tailor arranges a June wedding around his plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' only says the U is mixed in among the other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuptials is a formal plural noun for a marriage ceremony, so it fits wedding.

clue.text: Unknown country fills computer person with burning desire

indicators.note: to fill something is to go inside it, so these letters sit within the outer piece

blocks.note: PC is personal computer
y is an algebraic unknown
the Eastern European country

explanation.surface: Someone from an unidentified country is consumed by passion for their computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burning desire' reads as passion, but the definition is literal: a craving to set fires.
explanation.definitionFit: A pyromaniac has an obsessive urge to set fires, so a wry way to describe a burning desire.

clue.text: Film star in hat, beret, lazily dressed receiving Oscar

indicators.note: carelessly dressed means thrown together any old how, so the letters are disordered
to receive is to take in, so a letter is put inside the jumbled ones

blocks.note: taken as written
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A film star in casual headgear collects an Academy Award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lazily' is part of the fodder as well as the indicator's first word, a device setters allow. Oscar looks like the film award but is O.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth Taylor was a Hollywood actress, a star of Cleopatra and Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?

clue.text: Dog back from walkies pants

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so its final letter is kept

blocks.note: a boxer is a breed of dog
the last letter of walkies

explanation.surface: A dog comes back from its walk panting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like a verb for the dog's breathing but is a noun: underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers are loose men's underpants; in Britain pants means underwear.

clue.text: Examine piano covered with woodworm, maybe

indicators.note: something covered with another thing is surrounded by it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
a woodworm is an example of an insect, a beetle larva

explanation.surface: Check over a piano that may be riddled with woodworm.
explanation.walkthrough: INSECT wraps round P: IN-P-SECT gives INSPECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to look closely at something, a direct synonym for examine.

clue.text: City on the Douro bears essentially nice architectural feature

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letters are used
to bear something is to carry it, so the city holds the other piece within

blocks.note: Porto (Oporto) is the Portuguese city at the mouth of the Douro
the two middle letters of the word nice

explanation.surface: A Portuguese riverside city has a pleasant architectural feature.
explanation.walkthrough: The English name Oporto is common, but the city's own name Porto is what is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A portico is a roofed porch supported by columns, a classic feature of building design.

clue.text: Unbleached linen resourceful revolutionary collects

indicators.note: the word collects letters within itself, so the answer is sitting inside it
a revolution turns things round, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: four consecutive letters inside the word resourceful

explanation.surface: A clever revolutionary gathers up plain undyed linen.
explanation.walkthrough: URCE from resOURCEful, read backwards, is ECRU.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is the pale greyish-fawn colour of unbleached linen; the word also names such fabric.

clue.text: Frequency of spiritualist confronting doubters reducing by half

indicators.note: cutting something by half leaves only its first half of letters

blocks.note: a medium claims to contact the dead
waverers are people who doubt or hesitate

explanation.surface: How often a spiritualist faces sceptics whose numbers are halved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frequency' sounds like how often, but it is a radio frequency band; 'confronting' just sets one piece in front of the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Medium wave is a radio band, a range of broadcasting frequencies, so it names a frequency.

clue.text: Harry curls up with American, keeping love tender

indicators.note: to harry is to harass and disturb, so the letters are shaken up
to keep something is to hold it, so one letter goes inside the others

blocks.note: curls up, plus US for American
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Prince Harry snuggles up with an American and keeps their romance tender.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix CURLS UP + US into SCRUPULUS, then put O in before the last two letters. 'Harry' looks like the prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrupulous and tender both describe a conscience that is sensitive and careful about doing right.

clue.text: Stone, diamond, shown on quiz briefly

indicators.note: made brief means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: to pump someone is to quiz them; cut short
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A precious stone, a diamond, appears on a quick quiz show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone' tempts the solver to look for a gem alongside diamond, but the answer is a volcanic rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumice is a light porous volcanic rock used for scrubbing, so it is a kind of stone.

clue.text: Region of Europe, one familiar to Homer

blocks.note: first meaning: the historic area spanning Belgium and northern France
second meaning: Homer Simpson's devout next-door neighbour Ned in The Simpsons

explanation.walkthrough: Homer suggests the Greek poet, but it is Homer Simpson, whose neighbour is Ned Flanders.
explanation.definitionFit: Flanders is a Low Countries region, and Ned Flanders is the cartoon neighbour Homer knows well.

clue.text: Formal boycott over measure to evict 1000

indicators.note: evicting something throws it out, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: to black goods is to boycott them in a trade dispute
in music, measure means time or rhythm
M is the Roman numeral for 1000

explanation.surface: An official boycott of a plan to evict a thousand tenants.
explanation.walkthrough: TIME minus M gives TIE; 'over' places BLACK above it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Black tie is the dress code for formal evening events, so on an invitation it means formal.

clue.text: Wickedly heartless notice appears outside popular comprehensive

indicators.note: without its heart means the middle letter is taken out
sitting outside means wrapping round the other pieces

blocks.note: to spy is to notice; its centre letter goes
in means fashionable, popular
full means complete, comprehensive

explanation.surface: A cruel notice is posted outside a well-liked comprehensive school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comprehensive' suggests a British state school open to all abilities, but here it means complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinfully means in a wicked, morally wrong manner, so it is an adverb matching wickedly.

clue.text: Foolish to overlook lake when touring islands in Mediterranean destination

indicators.note: to overlook something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped
touring means travelling round, so the outer letters go round the inner ones

blocks.note: silly means foolish
L is the map abbreviation for lake
CI is the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: It's daft to skip the lake when sightseeing round Mediterranean islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The islands are not Mediterranean ones but the Channel Islands, Jersey and Guernsey off France.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicily is the large Italian island, a popular holiday spot in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Note bug going round, it brings sadness

indicators.note: turning round means the combined letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: soh is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
to bug a phone is to tap it

explanation.surface: A virus doing the rounds of the office brings misery.
explanation.walkthrough: SOH + TAP read backwards gives PATHOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathos is the quality in art or life that evokes pity and sorrow in an audience.

clue.text: Head pockets returning schoolmistresses' unisex clothes

indicators.note: the words clothe, or cover, the answer, so it lies within them
going back the way it came means the letters read backwards

blocks.note: letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Head teachers' pockets returning the mistresses' unisex garments.
explanation.walkthrough: SESUNIS from schoolmistreSSES' UNISex reads backwards as SINUSES. 'Clothes' looks like a noun but is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: The sinuses are air-filled cavities in the skull, literally pockets in the head.

clue.text: Nation needing energy to replace atomic plant

indicators.note: one thing replacing another means a letter swap within the word

blocks.note: the South Asian country
go means energy or drive
A is short for atomic, as in A-bomb

explanation.surface: A country that needs a new energy source in place of nuclear power stations.
explanation.walkthrough: In INDIA, GO takes the place of A. 'Plant' looks like a power station but is a living plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a shrub of the pea family whose leaves yield the blue dye of that name.

clue.text: Top barman ultimately dismissed over drink

indicators.note: the final letter is sent away, so the word is cut at its end

blocks.note: a cap is a top or lid
a composer writes music in bars, a 'bar man'; here the Italian opera composer
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: The head barman is sacked for what he did with a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barman' looks like a pub worker but is a writer of musical bars; Puccini loses his last I.
explanation.definitionFit: A cappuccino is an espresso coffee topped with frothed milk, a familiar café drink.

clue.text: Back new direction for something boring

indicators.note: going back means running from the end, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
a way is a direction, as in 'this way'

explanation.surface: Backing a fresh course of action because the old one was dull.
explanation.walkthrough: N + WAY read backwards gives YAWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A yawn is informal for something tedious, as in 'the film was a yawn'.

clue.text: Soft left politician, inspiring one

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so a letter is taken inside

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
MP is a member of Parliament
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A soft left-wing politician who motivates people.
explanation.walkthrough: L + MP, with MP breathing in I.
explanation.definitionFit: Limp means lacking firmness or stiffness, as of a floppy lettuce, so it is soft.

clue.text: Describe cycling to see part of rugby union match

indicators.note: letters going round in a cycle are moved from the front of the word to the back

blocks.note: to outline something is to describe it in broad terms

explanation.surface: Explain how bike riding relates to a rugby match.
explanation.walkthrough: The first three letters OUT move to the end of OUTLINE to give LINE-OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A line-out is the rugby union restart where forwards line up and jump for a ball thrown in from touch.

clue.text: In winter they'll hang out here abroad by cold bar briefly

indicators.note: made brief means shortened, so the word drops its last letter

blocks.note: ici is French for here
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
bar meaning except, as does less ('a year less a day')

explanation.surface: Winter is when people go to hang out in a cold bar abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hang out' looks like socialising but means literally dangling from eaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Icicles form in freezing weather and dangle from gutters and branches, so they are things that hang.

clue.text: It sets hard papers for Italians, suspect Scotsman conceded

indicators.note: what is conceded is given up, so those letters leave the fodder
something suspect is dodgy and not to be trusted as it stands, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
Ian is the Scottish form of John, the crossword's stock Scotsman

explanation.surface: A suspicious Scot gave ground over documents meant for Italians.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing I, A, N from ITALIANS leaves TLIAS; with PAPERS FOR that is the fourteen letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaster of Paris is a gypsum powder that, mixed with water, hardens quickly; used for casts and moulds.
